correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the four opposite edges, arclength normalization L=4(a+b), even angle function F_p(c), strict convexity for p>2 and strict concavity for 0<p<2. The collinear endpoint integrals cancel their unequal-segment terms exactly. For p<=2 an exact second-moment identity and Hölder imply the disk comparison; for p>2 sharp needle sup plus monotonicity of R(p) yield the unique critical exponent. The quadratic curvature remainder is integrated twice and for p=4 becomes the exact L,A formula. Rational checks confirm the polynomial identities; numerical quadrature is ancillary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a sharp upper envelope for p>2 over all centered parallelograms, a complete family-specific disk comparison through a new critical exponent, and a quartic exact area correction. The closest papers establish either the p<=2 disk upper bound (2311.18413), a p<=2 needle lower bound (2608.19851), or inclusion-monotonicity of weighted perimeters (2306.07770 and 2610.11677). These do not imply the reversed p>2 parallelogram inequality or its sharp threshold. Published indexed geometric findings on parallelogram chord statistics, widths, and radial mean bodies use mathematically different observables. Claim priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Potential older Sachs-era, general weighted-wire, or polygon-moment sources using equivalent formulas are not exhaustively accessible.
Published index retrieval is not a uniqueness certificate; no claim of historical priority is made.
The known p=2 equality and p<=2 disk comparison must not be attributed as new.

value.rationale: The p=3 boundary-moment disk inequality is a motivated open general convex-geometry question. This exact complete parallelogram test family has a sharp threshold p_c>3, quantifies strict separation at p=3, and shows genuinely nondegenerate violations after the cutoff. Its dimensionless full exponent phase diagram, angular extremizers and the exact quartic area defect identify structural geometric invariants; it is not a parameter substitution or isolated numerical benchmark.
